boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Boston University
boards.description: Boston University's linear campus along Commonwealth Avenue creates a unique late-night culture centered on accessible diners, student-run cafes, and reliable pizza spots that stay open well past midnight.

cards.title: T. Anthony's Pizzeria
cards.subtitle: The West Campus Pizza Staple
cards.notes: Visit this iconic spot across from West Campus for a late-night slice. It is famous for its walls covered in photos of BU athletes and its 2:00 AM closing time.
cards.short_summary: A legendary pizzeria across from West Campus known for its sports-themed decor and late-night service.
cards.evidence_claim: T. Anthony's Pizzeria is located across from Boston University and is open until 2:00 AM daily.
cards.source_title: T. Anthony | Pizza Restaurant & Delivery | Sports Bar | Boston, MA
cards.access_notes: Open daily until 2:00 AM.

cards.title: El Jefe's Taqueria
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Mexican on Comm Ave
cards.notes: Head here for burritos and tacos until the early morning. It is a popular destination for students looking for a substantial meal after a long study session.
cards.short_summary: A Mexican eatery on Commonwealth Avenue serving tacos and burritos until 3:00 AM.
cards.evidence_claim: El Jefe's Taqueria at Boston University is open daily from 8:00 AM to 3:00 AM.
cards.source_title: BOSTON UNIVERSITY | eljefestaqueria
cards.access_notes: Open daily until 3:00 AM.

cards.title: Warren Late Nite Café
cards.subtitle: Central Campus Dining Hall After-Hours
cards.notes: Use your dining points for late-night snacks at this central campus hub. It serves as a primary social and refueling spot for freshmen living in Warren Towers.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus late-night dining option located within the Warren Towers residential complex.
cards.evidence_claim: Warren Late Nite Café is an on-campus dining location at BU that provides late-night food options for students.
cards.source_title: The Fresh Food Co. at Warren Towers | Dining Services
cards.access_notes: Typically open until 2:00 AM during the academic semester.

cards.title: City Convenience
cards.subtitle: West Campus Midnight Essentials
cards.notes: Stop by this West Campus convenience store for snacks, drinks, or microwave meals. It is a go-to for students in the Claflin, Sleeper, and Rich Hall dorms.
cards.short_summary: A university-operated convenience store in West Campus providing late-night essentials.
cards.evidence_claim: City Convenience at Sleeper Hall is open daily until 1:00 AM.
cards.source_title: Locations & Hours | Dining Services
cards.access_notes: Open daily until 1:00 AM.

cards.title: Raising Cane's
cards.subtitle: The West Campus Chicken Run
cards.notes: Grab a Box Combo at this popular chicken finger chain. Its location near West Campus makes it a frequent stop for students before the 11:00 PM closing.
cards.short_summary: A popular fast-food chain on Commonwealth Avenue known for chicken fingers and signature sauce.
cards.evidence_claim: Raising Cane's at 949 Commonwealth Ave is open daily until 11:00 PM.
cards.source_title: Raising Cane's Chicken Fingers | Dining Services
cards.access_notes: Open daily until 11:00 PM.

cards.title: Insomnia Cookies
cards.subtitle: Warm Cookies Delivered Late
cards.notes: Order warm cookies for delivery or pick them up at the storefront. This is the classic choice for satisfying a late-night sweet tooth during finals week.
cards.short_summary: A bakery specializing in warm cookies delivered late into the night, popular with students.
cards.evidence_claim: Insomnia Cookies serves and delivers warm treats until late night, typically 1:00 AM or later.
cards.source_title: Insomnia Cookies | Warm Cookie Delivery
cards.access_notes: Open until 1:00 AM or later most nights.

cards.title: Tasty Burger
cards.subtitle: Fenway's Late-Night Grill
cards.notes: Walk toward Fenway for a burger and fries at this local favorite. It stays open until 2:00 AM, making it a reliable option for East Campus residents.
cards.short_summary: A popular burger joint near the Fenway area that serves food until 2:00 AM.
cards.evidence_claim: Tasty Burger at 1301 Boylston St is open daily until 2:00 AM.
cards.source_title: Locations | Tasty Burger
cards.access_notes: Open daily until 2:00 AM.

cards.title: Mugar Memorial Library
cards.subtitle: The 24-Hour Finals Hub
cards.notes: Find a quiet cubicle or a group table in BU's main library. During finals, it transitions to 24-hour operation to support all-night study sessions.
cards.short_summary: The primary library for Boston University, offering extended hours and 24-hour access during exams.
cards.evidence_claim: Mugar Memorial Library operates on a 24-hour schedule during study days and final exams.
cards.source_title: Mugar Memorial Library | BU Libraries
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours during finals; regular semester hours typically until 2:00 AM.

cards.title: Bay State Underground
cards.subtitle: East Campus Comfort Food
cards.notes: Visit the basement of the Yawkey Center for burgers and comfort food. It provides a cozy, subterranean atmosphere for late-night dining in East Campus.
cards.short_summary: A student-focused restaurant in the basement of the Yawkey Center offering comfort food.
cards.evidence_claim: Bay State Underground is a late-night dining location at 100 Bay State Road.
cards.source_title: Bay State Underground | Dining Services
cards.access_notes: Check seasonal hours; typically open late during the academic year.

cards.title: Domino's Pizza
cards.subtitle: The Reliable Delivery Run
cards.notes: Order a late-night pizza using your Convenience Points. This location is a staple for delivery to West Campus dorms during late-night gaming or studying.
cards.short_summary: A reliable pizza delivery option that accepts BU Convenience Points and stays open late.
cards.evidence_claim: Domino's Pizza at West Campus is open until 2:00 AM and accepts Convenience Points.
cards.source_title: Domino's Pizza | Dining Services
cards.access_notes: Open until 2:00 AM.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Discover the functional study nooks, specialized libraries, and quiet lounges across the Charles River Campus that Boston University students use for focused work and community connection.

cards.title: Theology Library Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Quiet study on the 2nd floor of 745 Commonwealth Ave
cards.notes: Visit this library for a peaceful, low-traffic environment. It is open to all BU students for quiet study and research during weekday business hours.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, specialized library on the second floor of the School of Theology building.
cards.evidence_claim: The School of Theology Library is open Monday-Friday 9 am – 5 pm and provides quiet study spaces for the BU community.
cards.source_title: School of Theology Library
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Friday, 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM. Closed on weekends.

cards.entity_name: Howard Thurman Center for Common Ground
cards.title: HTC Meditation Room
cards.subtitle: Quiet reflection space at 808 Commonwealth Ave
cards.notes: Use the meditation room for a silent break from classes. The space features moss-covered walls and is designed for quiet reflection and mindfulness.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated silent space for meditation and reflection within the Howard Thurman Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Howard Thurman Center features a meditation room with moss on the walls for student use.
cards.source_title: Take a Tour of the New and Expanded Howard Thurman Center for Common Ground
cards.access_notes: Open during regular HTC building hours; check official site for current semester schedule.

cards.title: Stone Science Silent Study
cards.subtitle: 4th floor of the CAS building
cards.notes: Head to the 4th floor of CAS for a strictly silent study environment. This non-circulating library is ideal for deep focus without the crowds of Mugar.
cards.short_summary: A silent research library located on the fourth floor of the College of Arts & Sciences.
cards.evidence_claim: The Stone Science Library provides silent study space and computer workstations during regular business hours.
cards.source_title: Stone Science Library
cards.access_notes: Open during weekday business hours; silent study policy strictly enforced.

cards.title: Music Listening Room
cards.subtitle: 2nd floor of Mugar Memorial Library
cards.notes: Study among the vinyl and scores in this specialized wing. It offers a unique atmosphere and silent study spaces away from the main library floors.
cards.short_summary: A specialized library wing on Mugar's second floor featuring music collections and quiet seating.
cards.evidence_claim: The Music Library on the second floor of Mugar includes a listening room and silent study spaces.
cards.source_title: Music Library
cards.access_notes: Accessible during Mugar Memorial Library's regular building hours.

cards.title: Astronomy Library Reading Room
cards.subtitle: 6th floor of the CAS building
cards.notes: Find this 'hidden' library by taking the center elevators in CAS to the 5th floor and walking up to the 6th. It offers silent study with a view.
cards.short_summary: A small, quiet library for astronomy and astrophysics located on the top floor of CAS.
cards.evidence_claim: The Michael D. Papagiannis Astronomy Library provides silent study space during normal hours of operation.
cards.source_title: Michael D. Papagiannis Astronomy Library
cards.access_notes: Unstaffed space; accessible via a specific stairwell from the CAS 5th floor.

cards.title: ASL Reading Room
cards.subtitle: 6th floor of Mugar Memorial Library
cards.notes: Take the north elevator to the 6th floor for one of the quietest spots in Mugar. The reading room is bright and typically less crowded than lower floors.
cards.short_summary: A specialized research library and reading room on the top floor of the main library.
cards.evidence_claim: The African Studies Library reading room is located on the 6th floor of Mugar Memorial Library.
cards.source_title: African Studies Library
cards.access_notes: Open during Mugar's regular hours; accessible via the north elevator.

cards.title: Pickering Library Study Lounge
cards.subtitle: Basement of 2 Silber Way
cards.notes: Study in the lower level of the Wheelock building. This library has an open floor plan with about 80 seats and separate rooms for collaborative work.
cards.short_summary: An education-focused library with collaborative and quiet study zones in East Campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Pickering Educational Resources Library offers open seating for about 80 people and reservable study rooms.
cards.source_title: Pickering Educational Resources Library
cards.access_notes: Open during academic year business hours; check library site for weekend availability.

cards.title: Pardee Library Team Rooms
cards.subtitle: 3rd floor of the Questrom School of Business
cards.notes: Reserve a team room for group projects. These spaces are located within the business school and offer a professional environment for collaborative work.
cards.short_summary: Collaborative study rooms and open seating within the Questrom School of Business.
cards.evidence_claim: Pardee Management Library offers silent open study spaces and four reservable team rooms for group work.
cards.source_title: Frederick S. Pardee Management Library
cards.access_notes: BU ID required for entry; rooms must be reserved in advance via the library website.

cards.title: ERC Study Lounge
cards.subtitle: 5th floor of 100 Bay State Road
cards.notes: Visit the 5th floor for open-concept study areas. You can also exchange your Terrier Card at the desk for a key to a private study room.
cards.short_summary: A student service center offering open lounges and private rooms for individual or peer study.
cards.evidence_claim: The Educational Resource Center (ERC) on the 5th floor of the Yawkey Center has open study areas and private rooms.
cards.source_title: Educational Resource Center
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Friday 9 am - 5 pm and Sunday 12 pm - 7 pm. Closed Saturdays.

cards.title: SEL Group Study Alcove
cards.subtitle: 1st floor of 38 Cummington Mall
cards.notes: Reserve this open-door alcove for quick two-person meetings. The library also offers quiet study seating in the lower level for longer sessions.
cards.short_summary: A focused library for STEM students with open seating and a reservable group alcove.
cards.evidence_claim: The Science & Engineering Library offers open study spaces on the 1st floor and a reservable Group Study Alcove.
cards.source_title: Science & Engineering Library
cards.access_notes: Open during regular building hours; alcove reservations are limited to 2 hours per day.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Discover social activities and campus spaces at Boston University that require no admission fees or purchases, from iconic outdoor lawns to cultural galleries and student-only wellness perks.

cards.title: Lounge at the BU Beach
cards.subtitle: Warren Alpert Mall
cards.notes: Relax on this grassy knoll behind Marsh Chapel; it is a prime spot for sunbathing and frisbee without any cost.
cards.short_summary: The BU Beach is a central campus lawn used for social gatherings and outdoor relaxation.
cards.evidence_claim: The BU Beach is open 24/7, 365 days a year, and students are free to access and enjoy the space at any time.
cards.source_title: A Day at the (BU) Beach | BU Today
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 to the public and students; no reservation or fee required for casual use.

cards.entity_name: Faye G., Jo, and James Stone Gallery
cards.title: View Art at Stone Gallery
cards.subtitle: 855 Commonwealth Avenue
cards.notes: Explore rotating contemporary art exhibitions in this professional gallery space located within the College of Fine Arts.
cards.short_summary: A professional exhibition space at BU featuring works by world-renowned artists and student thesis projects.
cards.evidence_claim: The Faye G., Jo, and James Stone Gallery has free admission and is open to the public.
cards.source_title: Faye G., Jo, and James Stone Gallery | College of Fine Arts
cards.access_notes: Open to the public during gallery hours; no tickets or purchase required.

cards.title: Join Coffee & Conversation
cards.subtitle: Howard Thurman Center
cards.notes: Participate in weekly Friday discussions about current events and social issues in a structured, inclusive environment.
cards.short_summary: A long-standing BU tradition of public dialogue and civil discourse held every Friday afternoon.
cards.evidence_claim: Coffee & Conversation is a free program open to all members of the BU community every Friday from 3:30pm to 5:00pm.
cards.source_title: Coffee & Conversation | Howard Thurman Center for Common Ground
cards.access_notes: Held Fridays 3:30 PM - 5:00 PM during the academic year; open to all BU students and staff.

cards.title: Swim at the FitRec Lazy River
cards.subtitle: 915 Commonwealth Avenue
cards.notes: Full-time students can use the competition pool and lazy river for recreation without paying a membership fee.
cards.short_summary: BU's primary fitness facility offers free access to pools and gym equipment for full-time students.
cards.evidence_claim: Membership for full-time students at Boston University is free and included in tuition.
cards.source_title: Student Membership | Fitness & Recreation Center
cards.access_notes: Requires a valid BU Terrier Card for entry; available during standard facility operating hours.

cards.title: Watch a Booth Theatre Play
cards.subtitle: 820 Commonwealth Avenue
cards.notes: Attend high-quality student theatre and opera productions for free by showing your university identification at the door.
cards.short_summary: A state-of-the-art performance space offering free admission to the BU community for School of Theatre shows.
cards.evidence_claim: All Boston University students, faculty, and staff receive free admission at the door with their BU ID to attend performances at Booth Theatre.
cards.source_title: Joan & Edgar Booth Theatre | College of Fine Arts
cards.access_notes: Free admission is subject to availability at the door; bring a valid BU ID.

cards.title: Study at Mugar Library
cards.subtitle: 771 Commonwealth Avenue
cards.notes: Utilize seven floors of study space, including a 24-hour computer lounge during finals, at no extra cost.
cards.short_summary: The main research library for the Charles River Campus, providing extensive free study areas for students.
cards.evidence_claim: Mugar Memorial Library is open to all students with a valid BU ID and offers various open study spaces.
cards.source_title: Study Rooms & Spaces | BU Libraries
cards.access_notes: Open daily; 24-hour access typically provided during final exam periods for students with BU ID.

cards.title: Gather at Marsh Plaza
cards.subtitle: 735 Commonwealth Avenue
cards.notes: Visit the heart of campus to see the Martin Luther King Jr. memorial or participate in outdoor university events.
cards.short_summary: A central plaza featuring the university seal and serving as a major hub for student gatherings and traditions.
cards.evidence_claim: Marsh Plaza is a public campus space used for various free community events and religious life programming.
cards.source_title: Students | Marsh Chapel & Religious Life
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible outdoor space; specific events like Community Dinners are free for students.

cards.title: Relax in Ziskind Lounge
cards.subtitle: George Sherman Union, 2nd Floor
cards.notes: Enjoy views of the Charles River from this spacious lounge located inside the student union building.
cards.short_summary: A large, comfortable lounge area in the George Sherman Union used for studying and social meetings.
cards.evidence_claim: The Ziskind Lounge is a 7,000 square foot space in the GSU available for student use and events.
cards.source_title: George Sherman Union | Events & Conferences
cards.access_notes: Open during GSU building hours; generally accessible to all students and visitors.

cards.title: Visit The Castle
cards.subtitle: 225 Bay State Road
cards.notes: Step inside this historic Tudor Revival mansion to admire the architecture or attend free university-hosted receptions.
cards.short_summary: A historic campus landmark that serves as an alumni center and venue for university events.
cards.evidence_claim: The Dahod Family Alumni Center at the Castle is a university-owned space that hosts various free community and alumni events.
cards.source_title: Dahod Family Alumni Center at the Castle
cards.access_notes: Primarily an event space; access is free for specific university-sanctioned events and receptions.

cards.title: Make Art at Create Space
cards.subtitle: Marsh Chapel Lower Level
cards.notes: Drop in on Tuesday afternoons for free, simple art projects designed to help students de-stress through creativity.
cards.short_summary: A weekly mindfulness and art program provided for free to the BU student community.
cards.evidence_claim: Create Space is held Tuesdays from 12-2 pm and offers simple, creative art projects for students at no cost.
cards.source_title: Students | Marsh Chapel & Religious Life
cards.access_notes: Tuesdays 12:00 PM - 2:00 PM during the academic year; open to all students.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: A curated selection of Boston University's most effective study environments, ranging from silent library floors to collaborative student centers across the Charles River Campus.

cards.title: Riverview Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Mugar Memorial Library, 1st Floor
cards.notes: Find a seat at the long tables for a quiet atmosphere with views of the Charles River. This silent zone is ideal for deep focus and long reading sessions.
cards.short_summary: A silent, scenic study hall on the first floor of BU's main library overlooking the Charles River.
cards.evidence_claim: The Riverview Reading Room is located on the 1st floor of Mugar Memorial Library and is designated as a silent study zone.
cards.source_title: Study Rooms & Spaces | Libraries - Boston University
cards.access_notes: Open during regular library hours; BU ID required for entry after 8:00 PM.

cards.title: Kilachand Hall 9th Floor Lounge
cards.subtitle: 91 Bay State Road
cards.notes: Access panoramic views of the Boston skyline and Fenway Park. This space features a quiet study room and a larger common area for residents.
cards.short_summary: A top-floor residential lounge offering 360-degree city views and dedicated quiet study areas.
cards.evidence_claim: The ninth floor study lounge at Kilachand Hall offers panoramic views and is available 24 hours a day to on-campus residents.
cards.source_title: Kilachand Hall | Boston University Housing
cards.access_notes: Restricted to on-campus residents; BU ID required for swipe access.

cards.title: Pardee Management Library
cards.subtitle: Questrom School of Business, 3rd Floor
cards.notes: Utilize the team rooms or open seating in this modern, well-lit space. It is specifically designed for business research and collaborative group work.
cards.short_summary: The primary library for the Questrom School of Business, featuring collaborative team rooms and quiet zones.
cards.evidence_claim: Pardee Management Library is located on the third floor of the Questrom School of Business and offers four reservable team rooms.
cards.source_title: Pardee Management Library – Open Study Spaces - Boston University
cards.access_notes: BU ID required for entry; team rooms must be reserved via the Student Study App.

cards.title: The Commons at HTC
cards.subtitle: 808 Commonwealth Ave, 2nd Floor
cards.notes: Study in an open, light-filled environment designed for community connection. The space includes a meditation room and various meeting nooks.
cards.short_summary: A spacious, multi-purpose common area in the Howard Thurman Center for Common Ground.
cards.evidence_claim: The Howard Thurman Center's new location at 808 Comm Ave features the Commons (Room 205) and other open study areas.
cards.source_title: What to Do at the New HTC | Howard Thurman Center for Common Ground
cards.access_notes: Open to all BU students during building hours; no reservation required for general seating.

cards.title: Educational Resource Center (ERC)
cards.subtitle: Yawkey Center, 5th Floor
cards.notes: Reserve a private room with a whiteboard for focused group sessions. The center also offers open-concept seating for individual work.
cards.short_summary: A student support hub on the 5th floor of the Yawkey Center offering private and open study spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The ERC at the Yawkey Center for Student Services has private rooms available on a first-come, first-served basis.
cards.source_title: The Best Places to Study for Finals - Boston University
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Friday 9 AM - 5 PM and Sunday 12 PM - 7 PM; BU ID required.

cards.title: Pickering Educational Resources Library
cards.subtitle: 2 Silber Way
cards.notes: Visit this quieter library in the Wheelock College building for a more intimate setting. It features a reservable quiet study room for up to 3 people.
cards.short_summary: A specialized library for education and human development with quiet, small-scale study options.
cards.evidence_claim: Pickering Library provides a reservable Quiet Study Room and a Classroom/Study Lounge that functions as a study space when not in use.
cards.source_title: Group Work and Quiet Study Spaces » BU Libraries | Boston University
cards.access_notes: Open during regular library hours; quiet study room bookings are limited to 3 hours.

cards.title: SEL Group Study Alcove
cards.subtitle: 38 Cummington Mall
cards.notes: Book this open-door alcove for quick collaborative meetings. The library also offers quiet study areas in the lower level for individual work.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated collaborative space within the Science & Engineering Library (SEL).
cards.evidence_claim: The Science & Engineering Library offers a Group Study Alcove that can be reserved for up to 2 hours per day.
cards.source_title: Science & Engineering Library - Boston University
cards.access_notes: Reservable for up to 2 people; open study space available on the 1st floor.

cards.title: School of Law Café
cards.subtitle: 765 Commonwealth Ave, 2nd Floor
cards.notes: Enjoy a bright, airy environment with floor-to-ceiling windows. While the library is restricted, the café is a popular spot for all students to work.
cards.short_summary: A spacious and naturally lit café area within the BU Law complex open for casual studying.
cards.evidence_claim: The School of Law Café on the second floor is a spacious, bright area with floor-to-ceiling windows used by students for studying.
cards.source_title: (Some of) The Amazing Places to Study on Campus - BU Blogs
cards.access_notes: Open to the general BU community; hours typically follow building operations.

cards.title: Computing & Data Sciences Nooks
cards.subtitle: 665 Commonwealth Ave
cards.notes: Explore the various nooks and open lounges in BU's newest landmark. The bottom two floors offer the best options for casual solo or group work.
cards.short_summary: Modern study lounges and nooks located within the 19-story 'Jenga' building.
cards.evidence_claim: The Duan Family Center for Computing & Data Sciences is open for learning and lounging, with study nooks on the bottom two floors.
cards.source_title: The Best Places to Study for Finals - Boston University
cards.access_notes: Open daily; Monday-Friday 7 AM - 10 PM, Weekends 8 AM - 10 PM.

cards.title: School of Theology Library
cards.subtitle: 745 Commonwealth Ave, 2nd Floor
cards.notes: Study in a historic setting featuring stained glass and a peaceful atmosphere. This library is known for being one of the quietest spots on campus.
cards.short_summary: A serene and historic library space known for its quiet environment and architectural beauty.
cards.evidence_claim: The School of Theology Library is located at 745 Commonwealth Ave and is recognized as a peaceful, quiet study location.
cards.source_title: School of Theology Library - Boston University
cards.access_notes: Open to all BU students; check website for specific seasonal hours.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Explore the real streets and corridors where Boston University students live, eat, and study beyond the official campus boundaries.

cards.title: The Heart of Allston Village
cards.subtitle: Harvard Avenue, Allston
cards.notes: Walk this corridor to find the city's highest concentration of student-friendly international eateries and thrift stores.
cards.short_summary: A major commercial spine in Allston known for diverse dining and high undergraduate residency.
cards.evidence_claim: Harvard Avenue is described as the spine of the Harvard Avenue Historic District and a major commercial and residential hub for students.
cards.source_title: Getting to Know Your Neighborhood: Allston | BU Today
cards.access_notes: Public city street; most businesses open late until 10 PM or midnight.

cards.title: Allston's Main Dining Strip
cards.subtitle: Brighton Avenue, Allston
cards.notes: Visit this block for a dense row of ramen shops, taquerias, and Korean BBQ spots popular for off-campus group dinners.
cards.short_summary: A vibrant thoroughfare in Allston featuring a wide variety of global cuisines and student housing.
cards.evidence_claim: Brighton Avenue is noted for its high concentration of restaurants including ramen, Italian, and vegetarian options.
cards.source_title: Getting to Know Your Neighborhood: Allston | BU Today
cards.access_notes: Public thoroughfare; high pedestrian activity throughout the day and evening.

cards.title: The Brookline Connection
cards.subtitle: Beacon Street, Brookline
cards.notes: Ride the Green Line C branch along this street to access quieter residential blocks and local coffee shops.
cards.short_summary: A major Brookline thoroughfare that serves as a primary residential area for BU upperclassmen.
cards.evidence_claim: Beacon Street in Brookline is highlighted as a popular area for BU students seeking off-campus housing and transit access.
cards.source_title: Getting to Know Your Neighborhood: Coolidge Corner | BU Today
cards.access_notes: Public street; primary route for the MBTA Green Line C branch.

cards.title: Gateway to the Fenway
cards.subtitle: Brookline Avenue, Fenway
cards.notes: Follow this road from Kenmore Square to reach the movie theater and major retail hubs in the Fenway district.
cards.short_summary: A key connector between Kenmore Square and the Fenway neighborhood's commercial center.
cards.evidence_claim: Brookline Avenue is part of the 'confusing convergence' at Kenmore Square and leads to the Fenway-Kenmore neighborhood.
cards.source_title: Getting to Know Your Neighborhood: Fenway-Kenmore | BU Today
cards.access_notes: Public street; connects Kenmore Square to the Longwood Medical Area.

cards.title: Beside the Green Monster
cards.subtitle: Lansdowne Street, Fenway
cards.notes: Walk behind Fenway Park's famous wall to experience the game-day energy and visit major concert venues.
cards.short_summary: A famous street bordering Fenway Park known for its entertainment venues and proximity to campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Lansdowne Street is described as having a 'crackle of excitement' and is home to House of Blues and other venues.
cards.source_title: Getting to Know Your Neighborhood: Fenway-Kenmore | BU Today
cards.access_notes: Public street; often closed to vehicles during Red Sox home games.

cards.title: Fenway's Modern Corridor
cards.subtitle: Boylston Street, Fenway
cards.notes: Explore this block for the Time Out Market food hall and modern study-friendly cafes near the Fens.
cards.short_summary: A redeveloped stretch of Boylston Street featuring upscale dining, retail, and park access.
cards.evidence_claim: Trendy restaurants line Boylston Street in the Fenway neighborhood, near the Time Out Market food hall.
cards.source_title: Fenway Park, Restaurants, Hotels, Nightlife - Boston Discovery Guide
cards.access_notes: Public street; food hall and retail hours typically extend to 10 PM.

cards.title: The Packard's Corner Hub
cards.subtitle: Commonwealth Avenue, Allston
cards.notes: Stock up on groceries at the large Star Market or Super 88 at this busy intersection where campus meets Allston.
cards.short_summary: The western extension of the main campus artery, serving as a major retail anchor for students.
cards.evidence_claim: Packard's Corner is the intersection of Harvard Street, Brighton Avenue, and Commonwealth Avenue, catering to students.
cards.source_title: Getting to Know Your Neighborhood: Allston | BU Today
cards.access_notes: Public street; Star Market is open 24 hours or late night depending on current policy.

cards.title: Historic Brownstone Row
cards.subtitle: Bay State Road, Boston
cards.notes: Walk this leafy, quiet street to see the historic brownstones that house many of BU's specialty residential communities.
cards.short_summary: A picturesque residential street in BU's East Campus known for its historic architecture.
cards.evidence_claim: Bay State Road is described as one of Boston's most picturesque streets, featuring charming brownstones.
cards.source_title: Bay State Road Brownstones - Housing - Boston University
cards.access_notes: Public residential street; very quiet compared to the parallel Commonwealth Avenue.

cards.title: The Iconic Citgo Gateway
cards.subtitle: Kenmore Square, Boston
cards.notes: Meet friends under the Citgo sign at this major transit hub that connects the East Campus to the rest of Boston.
cards.short_summary: A famous commercial square and transit hub at the eastern edge of the BU campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Kenmore Square is the 'culinary heart' of campus life and a major convergence of streets and transit.
cards.source_title: Getting to Know Your Neighborhood: Fenway-Kenmore | BU Today
cards.access_notes: Public square; major MBTA station for Green Line B, C, and D branches.

cards.title: The South Campus Link
cards.subtitle: St. Mary's Street, Brookline
cards.notes: Cross the bridge on this street to move between the main campus and the 'South Campus' residential area in Brookline.
cards.short_summary: A street connecting BU's central campus to its South Campus housing and the town of Brookline.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Mary's Street is a primary route for students walking from Commonwealth Avenue to the South Campus area.
cards.source_title: Getting to Know Your Neighborhood: Coolidge Corner | BU Today
cards.access_notes: Public street; includes a bridge over the MBTA tracks and the Mass Pike.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: From avoiding the Marsh Plaza seal to the annual physics pumpkin drop, Boston University's traditions are deeply rooted in its urban campus and spirited student body.

cards.title: Avoiding the Marsh Plaza Seal
cards.subtitle: Marsh Plaza
cards.notes: Walk around the bronze university seal in the center of Marsh Plaza; legend says stepping on it will prevent you from graduating in four years.
cards.short_summary: A campus superstition where students avoid stepping on the university seal to ensure timely graduation.
cards.evidence_claim: According to BU legend, undergraduate students who walk on the BU seal will not graduate within the regular four-year time period.
cards.source_title: Your favorite Terrier traditions | Alumni & Friends - Boston University
cards.access_notes: The seal is located in the open public plaza outside Marsh Chapel.

cards.entity_name: Metcalf Center for Science and Engineering
cards.title: The Annual Pumpkin Drop
cards.subtitle: Metcalf Science Center
cards.notes: Watch the Physics Department drop dozens of pumpkins filled with substances like ketchup and beans from the roof of the Metcalf Center every Halloween.
cards.short_summary: A messy Halloween tradition where the physics department drops pumpkins from a roof to demonstrate gravitational principles.
cards.evidence_claim: Each October, the Physics Department launches dozens of pumpkins off the roof of the Metcalf Center for Science and Engineering.
cards.source_title: Terrier Traditions | Admissions - Boston University
cards.access_notes: Spectators gather on the ground level outside the Metcalf Center.

cards.title: Lobster Night
cards.subtitle: Campus Dining Halls
cards.notes: Enjoy a full steamed lobster dinner at campus dining halls every September, a tradition celebrating New England culture since 1985.
cards.short_summary: An annual dining hall event where students are served fresh local lobster to welcome the new academic year.
cards.evidence_claim: Since 1985, BU has hosted an annual Lobster Night in every dining hall. Each student gets a full steamed Lobster plus all the fixings.
cards.source_title: Terrier Traditions | Admissions - Boston University
cards.access_notes: Available to students with meal plans; guests can pay with cash or credit.

cards.title: The Beanpot Tournament
cards.subtitle: TD Garden
cards.notes: Join the Dog Pound to cheer on the Terriers in this historic four-way hockey battle for Boston bragging rights held every February.
cards.short_summary: A prestigious annual ice hockey tournament between BU, BC, Harvard, and Northeastern.
cards.evidence_claim: Every February, the Men's and Women's Ice Hockey teams take on Northeastern, Harvard, and Boston College in a two-week tournament.
cards.source_title: Terrier Traditions | Admissions - Boston University
cards.access_notes: Tickets are required for entry to the tournament games at TD Garden.

cards.title: Marathon Monday
cards.subtitle: South Campus / Kenmore
cards.notes: Cheer on runners during the Boston Marathon as they pass through campus; classes are cancelled for the state holiday, Patriots' Day.
cards.short_summary: A city-wide holiday where students gather along the marathon route to support participants.
cards.evidence_claim: The last few miles of the Marathon go through BU's campus, making it an exciting and hard-to-miss tradition.
cards.source_title: Your favorite Terrier traditions | Alumni & Friends - Boston University
cards.access_notes: Public viewing areas are available along Commonwealth Avenue and Beacon Street.

cards.title: Senior Breakfast
cards.subtitle: Metcalf Ballroom
cards.notes: Attend this formal kickoff to Commencement season where the university announces the graduation speaker and honorary degree recipients.
cards.short_summary: A long-standing tradition for graduating seniors to celebrate their upcoming commencement.
cards.evidence_claim: The Senior Breakfast is a BU tradition that predates the George Sherman Union... photos from the 1952 and 1953 Senior Breakfasts show it goes back that long.
cards.source_title: Senior Breakfast 2026 | Dean of Students - Boston University
cards.access_notes: Open to graduating seniors; registration is typically required.

cards.title: Splash! Organization Fair
cards.subtitle: Nickerson Field
cards.notes: Explore over 450 student clubs and organizations at this massive involvement fair held on Nickerson Field every September.
cards.short_summary: The university's primary student organization fair held at the start of the fall semester.
cards.evidence_claim: Splash has been Boston University's involvement fair for all clubs, teams, and organizations around campus for over 20 years.
cards.source_title: Love Bugs, Stand-up, or Beatboxing? Find Your Club at Splash! | BU Today
cards.access_notes: Open to all BU students on Nickerson Field.

cards.title: Tagging the BU Rock
cards.subtitle: BU Beach
cards.notes: Look for the 'Greek Rock' near the BU Beach, which is constantly repainted by student organizations with layers of spray paint.
cards.short_summary: A large rock on campus that serves as a canvas for student groups to advertise and show spirit.
cards.evidence_claim: The Boston University Greek Rock—more commonly known as the BU Rock—is regularly spray painted by fraternities and sororities.
cards.source_title: Terrier Traditions | Admissions - Boston University
cards.access_notes: Located in the grassy area known as the BU Beach behind Marsh Chapel.

cards.title: Sitting with Rhett
cards.subtitle: Leventhal Admissions Center
cards.notes: Take a photo with the bronze statue of Rhett the Terrier, the university's mascot, located on a bench near the BU Beach.
cards.short_summary: A popular photo spot featuring a bronze statue of the university mascot.
cards.evidence_claim: The #RhettBench was installed in August 2019 to foster school spirit and create a new tradition... Rhett is patiently waiting for you to sit next to him.
cards.source_title: Five Terrier traditions we're in love with | Alumni & Friends - Boston University
cards.access_notes: The bench is located outdoors and accessible to the public.

cards.title: Global Days of Service
cards.subtitle: Various Locations
cards.notes: Participate in a month-long community service initiative every April, joining thousands of Terriers in volunteer projects worldwide.
cards.short_summary: An annual university-wide commitment to community service and volunteerism.
cards.evidence_claim: Every year in April, Boston University hosts Global Days of Service—a month of community service that brings alumni, students, faculty together.
cards.source_title: Global Days of Service 2026 - Boston University Alumni
cards.access_notes: Projects take place at various locations; registration is required to participate.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Boston University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: Build a plausible under-21-safe first-weekend sequence, not a ranking. Give each card one role in the sequence and use evergreen places or recurring behaviors rather than one-time events. Be conservative about hours, access, and travel time unless directly sourced.

cards.title: Unpack and Meet Your Floor
cards.subtitle: The start of your Terrier journey
cards.notes: Arrive at your assigned residence hall during your scheduled time slot to collect your Terrier Card and begin settling into your new Boston home.
cards.short_summary: Official move-in process for new students to settle into campus housing.
cards.evidence_claim: New student move-in for Fall 2026 is scheduled for Monday, August 24 and Tuesday, August 25.
cards.source_title: Fall 2026 On-Campus Orientation Schedule - Boston University
cards.access_notes: Requires pre-registered move-in time slot via the MyHousing portal.

cards.title: Mind the Step at the Seal
cards.subtitle: A central campus landmark
cards.notes: Walk through the heart of campus but be sure to step around the bronze BU Seal; legend says stepping on it prevents you from graduating in four years.
cards.short_summary: The central plaza of BU, home to a famous student superstition regarding the university seal.
cards.evidence_claim: Legend has it that if you walk across the BU Seal in Marsh Plaza, you will not graduate in four years.
cards.source_title: Why this BU tradition will have you avoiding a piece of Marsh Plaza | Dean of Students
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 as a public outdoor plaza.

cards.title: Fuel Up at Union Court
cards.subtitle: The hub of student life
cards.notes: Grab a meal at the GSU food hall, featuring options like Basho Sushi and Panda Express, while meeting up with new friends between orientation sessions.
cards.short_summary: The primary student union building housing a large food court and student services.
cards.evidence_claim: The George Sherman Union (GSU) is the hub of student life and houses a food court with multiple retail stations.
cards.source_title: George Sherman Union Hours and Information | Dean of Students
cards.access_notes: Building is open daily from 6 am to midnight during the academic year.

cards.title: Lounge at the BU Beach
cards.subtitle: A grassy retreat by the river
cards.notes: Relax on the 'beach'—a grassy knoll behind Marsh Chapel—where the sound of traffic on Storrow Drive mimics the sound of ocean waves.
cards.short_summary: A popular grassy area on campus used for sunbathing and socializing, despite having no sand.
cards.evidence_claim: The BU Beach is a grassy knoll formally known as the Warren Alpert Mall, popular for sunbathing and relaxing.
cards.source_title: Icons Among Us: The BU Beach | BU Today
cards.access_notes: Public outdoor space available during daylight hours.

cards.title: Activate Your Terrier Card
cards.subtitle: World-class fitness facilities
cards.notes: Bring your BU ID to FitRec to activate your membership and explore the pools, climbing wall, and multi-floor gym facilities.
cards.short_summary: The university's primary fitness center, free for full-time students.
cards.evidence_claim: Full-time students have automatic access to FitRec included in tuition; they must sign a waiver on their first visit.
cards.source_title: Students | Fitness & Recreation Center
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Thursday 6 am - 10 pm; weekend hours vary.

cards.title: Find Your Community at Splash
cards.subtitle: The ultimate club recruitment event
cards.notes: Head to Nickerson Field to browse hundreds of student organizations, from club sports to cultural groups, and sign up for mailing lists.
cards.short_summary: BU's massive semiannual fair for student clubs and organizations.
cards.evidence_claim: Splash is BU's club fair held on Nickerson Field on the first Saturday of September during Orientation Week.
cards.source_title: Find Your Club at Splash! | BU Today
cards.access_notes: Typically held from noon to 2:30 pm on the first Saturday of the semester.

cards.title: Scope Out a Study Spot
cards.subtitle: The main campus library
cards.notes: Explore the stacks and find your preferred floor for future study sessions; the higher floors offer quieter environments for deep focus.
cards.short_summary: The primary research library for the Charles River Campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Mugar Memorial Library is the largest library on campus and offers various study spaces including reservable rooms.
cards.source_title: Study Rooms & Spaces | Libraries
cards.access_notes: Open until midnight most nights; requires BU ID for entry after hours.

cards.title: Stroll the Riverfront Path
cards.subtitle: Scenic views of the Boston skyline
cards.notes: Cross the footbridge near the BU Beach to access the Esplanade for a walk or run along the Charles River with views of Cambridge.
cards.short_summary: A long riverside park accessible via pedestrian bridges from the BU campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Esplanade stretches along the Charles River and is accessible from BU via pedestrian footbridges.
cards.source_title: Map & Directions - The Esplanade Association
cards.access_notes: Open from dawn to dusk daily.

cards.title: Explore Art for Free
cards.subtitle: World-class museum access
cards.notes: Take a short trip to the MFA and use your BU ID for free admission to explore one of the most comprehensive art collections in the world.
cards.short_summary: A major art museum offering free admission to BU students.
cards.evidence_claim: BU students receive free membership and admission to the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston with a valid BU Student ID.
cards.source_title: Art Memberships & Discounts | Office for the Arts
cards.access_notes: Check MFA website for current hours; typically closed Tuesdays.

cards.title: Catch a Terrier Event
cards.subtitle: Home of BU Hockey
cards.notes: Visit the arena to pick up your student sports pass or attend a welcome event to experience the energy of the Terrier community.
cards.short_summary: A multi-purpose arena that serves as the home for BU hockey and major campus events.
cards.evidence_claim: Agganis Arena is the place for first-year students to show BU pride and use their Sports Pass for athletic events.
cards.source_title: First Year Students - Agganis Arena
cards.access_notes: Event times vary; ticket office is located at 925 Commonwealth Ave.
